scope: Qualified exact upstream FFmpeg 9.0.2 release, private optimised gcc13 minimal build with libx264, FFV1 and raw RGB plus the required PNG-independent encode/decode and Matroska/MP4 formats, without assembly or network; target release archive signature verified. H.264 and FFV1 version1 whole-frame RGB, timed sprite sheet, nine nonuniform image shapes, native stage input bindings, media requirements and offline rejection verified. Retained FFmpeg6.1.1 compatibility passes; no exhaustive codec/API coverage. Existing-video ingestion qualified on exact 9.0.2: silent single-stream MP4/H264 yuv420p and Matroska/FFV1 bgr0, full source cadence/metadata checks, exclusive presentation-frame selection/retiming, native default MP4 edit-list case and bound source probe/decode. Independent per-frame RGB checks include 72-frame 128x72 source clips and changed ranges/rates/inputs; no general editing, audio, rotation, fractional-rate or colour-management qualification. A second exact-9.0.2 build (official source, static libx264 stable-branch commit b35605a, no assembly, no network) re-ran the recipes and added independent profile/BT.601 colour-declaration readback, 600/601-frame, B-frame, adaptor-published H.264 and damaged-container cases; see the 2026-10-25 note. FFV1 level 1 payload corruption without decoder errors is an undetectable native limit. Allocation 39 adds the muxReview operation on exact 9.0.2 with libx264 (static, no assembly, no network): Matroska FFV1 (copy) + PCM16 (copy) + SubRip (copy) with independent native membership, whole-frame video, PCM byte and caption text/millisecond readbacks, an exact-rational duration policy, and wrong-source/extra-stream/malformed/tamper/timeout/cancellation probes; no AAC, H.264, WebVTT, burn-in or arbitrary stream coverage. Allocation 48 adds extractAudio on exact 9.0.2 with libx264 (static, no assembly, no network): one AAC-LC stream of an MP4/M4A decoded natively to PCM16, with a bounded audio-frame probe (decoded nb_samples with contiguous timestamps, not packets x 1024), host canonical WAV, forced mov demuxer and file protocol, enable_drefs 0, every PCM byte of a fresh decode compared, and mono/stereo/odd-length/one-frame/rate/H.264+AAC, refusal, forgery, timeout and cancellation probes; no HE-AAC, surround, fragmented MP4, other codecs or authenticated-capture coverage. Official source check 2026-10-25: 9.0.2 released 2026-09-18 is the latest stable release; the mov demuxer options enable_drefs and use_absolute_path are documented and off by default. Review-30 repair of extractAudio: native-stage faults are classified by cause (runtime failures RUNNER_FAILED, source diagnostics INVALID_RESOURCE, output-cap hits RESOURCE_LIMIT), probe output capped at 4 MiB and the frame listing bounded at 17600 packets / 17500 frames as refusals (large-tag and decode-cap native probes); no 960-sample native source and no exhaustive AAC-LC coverage. Fresh integrated native development-kit cases were repeated against the current source; consult the registered receipt for exact cases and recorded runtimes. This refresh does not broaden the documented operation or runtime-support scope. Fresh native development-kit cases were repeated on the integrated source; the registered receipt records exact cases and runtimes. This refresh alone does not broaden operation scope.
acceptance: Run tools/qualify_media_geospatial.py with target FFmpeg and FFprobe; require video decode, frame-count and dimensions verification.

Run tools/qualify_ffmpeg_deliverable.py and the native adaptor conformance kit on the exact target release; require all nine shape full-RGB readbacks, H.264/sheet acceptance, unmet intent gates and replaced encoded video with refreshed ordinary publication metadata rejection.

Run tools/qualify_ffmpeg_video.py with target FFmpeg/FFprobe; require every source and selected output frame independently compared, long clip baseline/variant, H264 input/output, actual MP4 edit-list presentation, source retention/reuse, dishonest receipt/binding/selection and timeout probes, default B-frame and adaptor-published H.264 sources, 600-frame acceptance with 601-frame RESOURCE_LIMIT for both codecs, and truncated/corrupt MP4/MKV INVALID_RESOURCE (FFV1 level 1 silent corruption recorded as a limit).

Run tools/qualify_ffmpeg_review.py with target FFmpeg/FFprobe; require three-stream membership, decoded video frames, PCM bytes and caption cues independently equal to literal sources, deterministic output bytes, the one-frame duration boundary, wrong-source/malformed/unsupported audio and caption rejection, cancellation/timeout/incomplete handling, refreshed-metadata tamper rejection and the encodeVideo-to-muxReview workflow handoff.

Run tools/qualify_ffmpeg_audio.py with target FFmpeg/FFprobe; require canonical WAV PCM bytes equal to an independent native decode for mono, stereo, odd-length, one-frame, rate-bound and H.264+AAC sources, priming-independent frame counts, every refusal, coherent forgery, planted-runtime, timeout and cancellation probe, and the SoX conform handoff.
